title: Tumour markers — uses and misuses

guidelineVersions: NICE NG151 Colorectal cancer (2020, current online guidance)
NICE NG85 Pancreatic cancer in adults (2018)
NICE CSG2 Improving Outcomes in Urological Cancers (accessed 12 October 2026)
NICE NG12 Suspected cancer: recognition and referral (updated 15 April 2026)
NICE CG122 Ovarian cancer: recognition and initial management (2011, updated 2026)

brief.scenario: You are the core surgical trainee. Card A: 62-year-old post-curative colorectal resection, CEA 2.1 then 4.6 then 8.7 µg/L at successive visits. Card B: obstructive jaundice, CA19-9 480 U/mL, pancreas imaging pending. Card C: 27-year-old with solid testicular lesion on ultrasound; AFP 160 kIU/L and β-hCG raised. Card D: 65-year-old with 2 months of early satiety, bloating and pelvic discomfort, CA125 28 IU/mL. Card E: asymptomatic adult requests a “full cancer blood-marker screen”.
brief.task: Interpret a sequence of five short tumour-marker results, describe which markers support surveillance or diagnosis, and identify tests that cannot establish malignancy on their own. Explain a new symptom-driven request to the examiner.

beforeYouWalkIn.frame: Oncology MDT teaching room; serial report cards
beforeYouWalkIn.trap: Treating any tumour marker as a definitive cancer test and using the old universal CA125 35 IU/mL threshold despite NICE 2026 changes.
beforeYouWalkIn.firstMove: These tests have different roles. I will not infer malignancy from a single marker result; I will interpret each in the clinical and imaging pathway.

flow: State clinical frame and identify the report’s key abnormality.
Interrogate the missing context and interpret evidence.
Explain differential and limitations, without overdiagnosis.
State safe pathway, investigations and specialist escalation.
Handle the new cue and close with explicit next steps.

grid.label: Opening and interpretive rule
grid.fail: Equates elevated marker with proven malignancy.
grid.borderline: Recognises markers may be non-specific but does not use a case-based plan.
grid.pass: States markers supplement history, imaging and histology, not stand-alone diagnoses.
grid.high: Contrasts screening, triage, prognostic use and surveillance with examples.

grid.label: CEA in colorectal follow-up
grid.fail: Uses CEA alone to diagnose recurrence.
grid.borderline: Notices rise but plans only repeat CEA indefinitely.
grid.pass: Identifies rising postoperative CEA as reason to review trend and complete surveillance assessment with CT per NG151.
grid.high: Notes a normal CEA does not exclude recurrence and confirms 3-year surveillance context.

grid.label: CA19-9 limitations
grid.fail: Calls CA19-9 definitive pancreatic cancer evidence.
grid.borderline: Names pancreatic association but no limitations.
grid.pass: Says CA19-9 cannot replace pancreatic-protocol CT and specialist assessment.
grid.high: Explains elevation also occurs with benign biliary obstruction, and interpretation depends on jaundice and imaging.

grid.label: AFP and β-hCG use
grid.fail: Labels any raised AFP as hepatocellular carcinoma.
grid.borderline: Mentions testicular germ cell tumours without marker or imaging context.
grid.pass: States AFP and β-hCG help classify germ-cell tumours alongside examination and ultrasound.
grid.high: Separates AFP/β-hCG patterns and recognises markers should be obtained before treatment when germ-cell cancer is suspected.

grid.label: CA125 primary-care pathway
grid.fail: Uses CA125 35 for every age including a 65-year-old.
grid.borderline: Knows ovarian symptoms and CA125 but cannot state updated age threshold.
grid.pass: For a 65-year-old with persistent symptoms, identifies the NG12 age 60–69 threshold (CA125 24 IU/mL or greater) for urgent, direct access abdominal and pelvic ultrasound.
grid.high: States age-specific 2026 thresholds and cautions against falsely reassuring symptomatic patients below thresholds.

grid.label: Secondary care ovarian assessment
grid.fail: Treats CA125 28 as conclusive ovarian cancer.
grid.borderline: Requests pelvic imaging but has no differential.
grid.pass: Requests pelvic ultrasound and gynaecology assessment with clinical context; no diagnosis from CA125 alone.
grid.high: Recognises secondary-care CA125 and risk stratification differ from a screening test.

grid.label: False positives and negatives
grid.borderline: Gives one false positive cause only.
grid.pass: Describes inflammatory, hepatobiliary and benign causes of elevations and false-negative results.
grid.high: Explains why marker trends can mislead without consistent testing and radiological correlation.

grid.label: Communication and MDT
grid.fail: Informs patient they have cancer based on blood test.
grid.borderline: Says marker is abnormal without discussing next investigation.
grid.pass: Communicates uncertainty, imaging and MDT need; avoids premature diagnosis.
grid.high: Provides proportionate risk discussion and specific follow-up, documentation and safety net.

grid.label: Curveball and synthesis
grid.fail: On patient request for a whole-body marker screen, orders a panel.
grid.borderline: Discourages screening but gives no alternative.
grid.pass: Declines indiscriminate marker screening, offers symptom-directed evaluation instead.
grid.high: Returns to symptoms and appropriate age-specific or organ-specific pathways, explaining harms of false positives.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: First principle: how will you interpret these tests?

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: They support a clinical decision but do not prove or rule out cancer on their own.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: Card A: CEA 2.1, 4.6 then 8.7 after colorectal surgery.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: The rise warrants surveillance review including imaging and MDT discussion, not a diagnosis from CEA alone.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: Card B: CA19-9 480 in a jaundiced patient.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: This alone cannot diagnose pancreatic cancer. I would prioritise pancreatic and biliary imaging.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: Card C: testicular mass; AFP and β-hCG elevated.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: These support a germ-cell tumour work-up with testicular ultrasound, staging and specialist referral.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: Card D: a symptomatic 65-year-old has CA125 28. Is this below the threshold?

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: No. The updated NG12 threshold for age 60–69 is 24 or above, so she needs an urgent, direct access ultrasound of the abdomen and pelvis.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: What should secondary care do if ovarian cancer is suspected?

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Assess clinically, review pelvic ultrasound and marker context, and involve the appropriate gynaecology pathway.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: Could apparently normal or high markers mislead?

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Yes. Both false positives and false negatives occur, so results need clinical context.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: How do you explain these results to a patient?

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: I would explain that the markers are clues and describe the next investigation without declaring cancer.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: An asymptomatic adult requests a full tumour-marker panel for reassurance.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: I would not order an indiscriminate panel. I would assess their concerns and offer appropriate, evidence-based screening or symptom assessment.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: First principle: how will you interpret these tests?

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: I distinguish triage from monitoring and staging: test meaning depends on disease, symptoms, assay and imaging.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: Card A: CEA 2.1, 4.6 then 8.7 after colorectal surgery.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: This trend is concerning but non-specific. NG151 uses CEA with CT in the first three years; I would review timing, serial trends and chest–abdomen–pelvis imaging.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: Card B: CA19-9 480 in a jaundiced patient.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: CA19-9 is unreliable as a solitary diagnostic marker, particularly with biliary obstruction; clinical assessment and pancreatic-protocol imaging lead the pathway.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: Card C: testicular mass; AFP and β-hCG elevated.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: AFP, β-hCG and LDH can inform suspected testicular malignancy, but correlation with ultrasound and histology is crucial; avoid unplanned trans-scrotal biopsy.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: Card D: a symptomatic 65-year-old has CA125 28. Is this below the threshold?

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: NICE April 2026 thresholds are age-specific. At 65, 28 exceeds the 24 IU/mL primary-care investigation threshold. With persistent symptoms, she needs an urgent, direct access abdominal and pelvic ultrasound, not reassurance.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: What should secondary care do if ovarian cancer is suspected?

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: CG122 distinguishes secondary-care evaluation from population screening; pelvic imaging and clinical assessment determine escalation and tissue/pathology planning.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: Could apparently normal or high markers mislead?

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Yes. Inflammation, hepatobiliary disease and benign conditions can elevate markers; a normal result does not end investigation of concerning symptoms.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: How do you explain these results to a patient?

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: I would discuss uncertainty honestly, specify the planned investigation and expected communication of results, and address the patient’s understanding and anxiety.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: An asymptomatic adult requests a full tumour-marker panel for reassurance.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: A broad marker panel risks misleading false positives and false reassurance. I would take a risk-focused history, discuss established screening and avoid indiscriminate testing.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: Please summarise your next action in one sentence.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: I will use symptom-directed assessment and validated screening, not a blanket marker panel.

failures.move: Calls rising CEA definitive recurrence and withholds imaging.
failures.consequence: May misdirect treatment and delay confirmation.

failures.move: Uses universal 35 IU/mL to dismiss a symptomatic 65-year-old with CA125 28.
Orders indiscriminate marker screening and falsely reassures from normal values.
failures.consequence: False positives, unnecessary testing and missed clinical assessment.

recovery.when: If you treated the CA19-9 result as a diagnosis
recovery.line: I was treating the CA19-9 result as a diagnosis; with jaundice I must interpret it alongside pancreatic-protocol imaging, not in isolation.

recovery.when: If you used an obsolete CA125 threshold
recovery.line: I used an obsolete CA125 threshold. NG12 now has an age-60–69 threshold of 24 IU/mL, so this patient with persistent symptoms needs an urgent abdominal and pelvic ultrasound.

knowledge.fact: After potentially curative non-metastatic colorectal surgery, CEA and CT are components of surveillance for the first three years.
A rising CEA is not a standalone diagnosis of recurrent colorectal cancer.
Pancreatic cancer investigation and staging rely on imaging and multidisciplinary assessment; CA19-9 is not a substitute.
AFP, β-hCG and LDH are markers included in evaluation of suspected testicular germ-cell malignancy.

NG12 (April 2026) uses age-specific CA125 thresholds for people aged 40 or over with persistent symptoms: at 60–69, CA125 24 IU/mL or greater means an urgent, direct access ultrasound of the abdomen and pelvis.
Secondary-care suspected ovarian cancer assessment includes CA125 and pelvic ultrasound, with AFP and β-hCG added in people under 40 where appropriate.

recall.think: A marker is a clinical clue, not a histological diagnosis.
recall.say: “I will interpret the trend alongside symptoms, imaging and the cancer pathway.”
do: Use CEA for colorectal follow-up; assess jaundice with imaging; use AFP/β-hCG with testicular ultrasound; investigate ovarian symptoms appropriately.

numbers.meaning: CA125 thresholds (age 40+, persistent symptoms) for urgent, direct access abdominal and pelvic ultrasound (NG12 table 1, April 2026)

recall.trap: Never order a blanket marker screen or apply 35 IU/mL to every age in 2026.
recall.finish: Identify next investigations and communicate uncertainty without falsely diagnosing cancer.
